name: Josefina 'Pepa' Archuleta
equipment: Buckskin coat, fringed and smoke-dark, made by her grandmother in Conejos, over a man's linen shirt
Army revolver (Colt Single Action, nickel-plated, bought with her first year's wages riding shotgun), 6 loaded
Repeating rifle (Winchester 1873, with a brass tack in the stock for every holdup she has stopped: there are five)
Bowie knife in a beaded sheath
A coach horn from the Argent and Fairplay stage line, which she was told to return and did not
Saddle, bridle and a Navajo saddle blanket she bought in Santa Fe
Rope, canteen, bedroll, a bag of piñon nuts and a tin of her mother's chile
A letter from a lawyer in Pueblo about her family's land grant, read so often the folds are wearing through
Riding horse: a buckskin gelding called Pinto Viejo, who is not a pinto and resents it
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: she speaks English and Spanish natively, knows the trails and towns of the San Luis Valley and northern New Mexico, and has advantage on Persuasion and Insight checks with people who live along the border, of either side; she can always find a guide, a ford or a bed there)

Quick Draw (Gunslinger: advantage on initiative and on the draw in a showdown; when she rolls initiative and is not surprised she draws a Sidearm as part of the roll, and drawing or holstering never costs her an interaction)
Gun Hand: Fast Hands (Gunslinger: she reloads a revolver as a bonus action, two rounds, and swaps a spare cylinder as a bonus action)
Fan the Hammer (Gunslinger, 2nd level: she can fan up to 4 rounds in one action, the first without disadvantage; fanned shots add no ability modifier to damage)
Style: Trick Shooter (Gunslinger, 3rd level: her called shots take −2 instead of −5, and she can shoot a weapon, a rope, a lamp, a fuse or a hat off a head without any chance of hitting the person)

The Mail Road (Stage Driver background: every station keeper, hostler and driver on the Argent and Fairplay line knows her; she can get a fresh team, a meal and the road news at any stage station, and drive any team that can be driven)

personality.traits: I talk very little and laugh at the wrong moments. I never sit with my back to a door, and I never let anyone else drive a team I could drive myself.
personality.ideals: Pay what you owe, protect what you are paid to protect, and never let a man think you are afraid of him, even when you are.
personality.bonds: My family's land on the Conejos, which a man in Pueblo with a new survey and an old grudge says is his. Every dollar I earn goes to the lawyer fighting him. And Hester Ruane, who hired a woman to ride shotgun when nobody else would.
personality.flaws: I am proud and quick to take offence, and I would rather be shot than be laughed at. I have a temper I keep in a box, and the box has a weak lid.

appearance: A small, wiry Hispana of twenty-eight with a sunburned face, a broken nose that healed crooked, black hair in one long braid and very still dark eyes. She wears a flat-crowned black hat, the buckskin coat, a split riding skirt over boots, and the nickel Colt high on her right hip. She sits a horse like a part of it and stands like she would rather be sitting one.
backstory: Pepa Archuleta grew up on her family's farm and sheep range on the Conejos River in the San Luis Valley, part of a Mexican land grant her great-grandfather helped settle, which the courts have been arguing about since Colorado became a territory. Her father drove freight to Santa Fe and taught her to shoot and to drive six horses; when he died she took over his route, and when the freight business died she rode shotgun on the Argent and Fairplay stage, the only woman on the line, and stopped five holdups in two years. Last year Hester Ruane hired her to guard the ore wagons from the Argent Reduction Works over the pass, at a man's wages. When the railroad comes, the ore wagons stop, and so does the job. Mrs. Ruane has asked her to ride the first silver train and see it safe to Hollowell Junction, and has promised her a place with the railroad's express guards afterward if she does. She is not sure she wants to spend her life in a box on wheels. She is sure she wants to be paid.
